items.title: Colapinto has a confirmed carry-over drop; Lindblad and Hadjar report PU penalties
items.summary: Colapinto's five-place carry-over sanction is established by FIA Azerbaijan Document 66. The Race reports Racing Bulls announcing a back-of-grid start for Lindblad and Hadjar expecting five places. No Sepang stewards' rulings for those planned PU changes were found in the twelve-document review before FP1.
items.why_it_matters: Distinguish an issued decision from a team or driver announcement. Neither establishes a final starting position before qualifying and the official grid.

items.title: FIA declares a Heat Hazard for Sunday's race
items.summary: FIA Document 3 declares a Heat Hazard under Article B1.5.10 because the official forecast Heat Index exceeds 31.0 degrees Celsius at some point during the Race. The venue is Sepang, with Sunday's start at 15:00 MYT / 10:00 Tallinn.
items.why_it_matters: This is an official declaration, not a generic weather warning. Do not equate Heat Index with ambient temperature or infer cooling-system requirements from temperature alone.

items.title: Pirelli details Sepang surface work before its return
items.summary: Pirelli reports that Sepang's Turns 6–12 section was resurfaced in 2023, with further work around Turn 9, and that additional levelling and cleaning took place from early September 2026. Engineers still assess the overall surface characteristics as similar to 2017. The event poster rates tyre stress and abrasion 4/5, nominates C2/C3/C4 and estimates 22.5 seconds pit-stop loss.
items.why_it_matters: Do not describe the circuit as untouched since 2017: sections have been resurfaced and levelled. Keep that work distinct from Pirelli's current assessment of similar overall surface characteristics; tyre behaviour for this generation remains unknown until practice.

items.title: FIA confirms 14 upgrade items, including Mercedes' seven-part package
items.summary: FIA Document 12, issued Friday at 10:03 MYT, lists seven Mercedes items, two Racing Bulls items and one each for McLaren, Red Bull, Ferrari, Haas and Alpine. Williams, Aston Martin, Audi and Cadillac explicitly submitted no updates.
items.why_it_matters: All eleven teams now have reviewed declarations and inline readers on the Upgrades page. Counts refer to declared component rows, not lap-time gain or a guarantee that both cars ran every item.
